company.name: Harvest Lane
company.description: An online grocery marketplace. A third of carts are abandoned at checkout, and the team suspects the page.

title: Harvest Lane: the checkout page
brief: This is the checkout page of Harvest Lane, as it ships today. Use it like a customer would, then mark every usability problem you find: click the part of the screen, name the problem and say what you saw. Some parts are fine, and flagging them counts against you.

issues.explanation: The delivery options use internal jargon ('SLA-72', 'P1 courier', 'tier 2 surcharge') and never say when the order arrives or what it costs, which is all the customer wants to know.
issues.fix: Describe each option by arrival date and price, in the customer's words.

issues.explanation: Applying a promo code gives no sign of success or failure, and the total does not visibly change. People retype the code or leave to search for another one.
issues.fix: Confirm the code inline, show the discount as a line in the summary, and explain clearly when a code is not valid.

issues.explanation: The total sits in the middle of the list, in the same style as every other line. The number people must check before paying is the hardest one to find.
issues.fix: Put the total last, separated from the lines above, in larger and bolder type.

issues.explanation: The refund deadline is in pale grey, tiny text that fails contrast guidelines. People only discover it after the 48 hours have passed.
issues.fix: Show policies that cost the customer money in readable text with enough contrast.

hidden.principle: Judge a screen by the user's goal: every element should help them reach it, say clearly what will happen, and tell them what did happen.

props.text: Missing or damaged items must be reported within 48 hours or refunds are not possible.

userGoal: A Harvest Lane customer with a full cart wants to choose delivery, pay and get their order.
